arxiv-2108-00861.title: Revisiting dissipative motion of a spinning heavy symmetric top and the rise of the top by friction
arxiv-2108-00861.creator: V. Tanrıverdi
arxiv-2108-00861.description: Abstract The dissipative motion and the rise of a heavy symmetrical top with a hemispherical peg are studied. A model taking the fixed point of the top as the center of the peg is considered when the top completely slips and the rolling motion is ignored. This is different from existing models like Jellet’s one.

arxiv-2112-14216.title: Casper: Accelerating Stencil Computations using Near-Cache Processing
arxiv-2112-14216.creator: Alain Denzler 1 Geraldo F. Oliveira 1 Nastaran Hajinazar 1,2 Rahul Bera 1 Gagandeep Singh 1 Juan Gómez-Luna 1 Onur Mutlu 1 1 ETH Zürich 2 Simon Fraser University
arxiv-2112-14216.description: Abstract Stencil computations are commonly used in a wide variety of scientific applications, ranging from large-scale weather prediction to solving partial differential equations. Stencil computations are characterized by three properties: (1) low arithmetic intensity, (2) limited temporal data reuse, and (3) regular and predictable data access pattern.

arxiv-2305-15187.title: Using Models Based on Cognitive Theory to Predict Human Behavior in Traffic: A Case Study
arxiv-2305-15187.creator: Julian F. Schumann, Aravinda Ramakrishnan Srinivasan, Jens Kober, Gustav Markkula, Arkady Zgonnikov
arxiv-2305-15187.description: Abstract The development of automated vehicles has the potential to revolutionize transportation, but they are currently unable to ensure a safe and time-efficient driving style. Reliable models predicting human behavior are essential for overcoming this issue. While data-driven models are commonly used to this end, they can be vulnerable in safety-critical edge cases.

arxiv-2401-10972.title: Clustering Molecular Energy Landscapes by Adaptive Network Embedding
arxiv-2401-10972.creator: Paula Mercurio, Di Liu
arxiv-2401-10972.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Paula Mercurio, Di Liu. In order to efficiently explore the chemical space of all possible small molecules, a common approach is to compress the dimension of the system to facilitate downstream machine learning tasks. Towards this end, we present a data driven approach for clustering potential energy landscapes of molecular structures by applying recently developed Network Embedding techniques, to obtain latent variables defined through the embedding function.

arxiv-2404-12687.title: Electronic structure and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering in Ca 3 Ru 2 O 7
arxiv-2404-12687.creator: V.N. Antonov, D.A. Kukusta, L.V. Bekenov
arxiv-2404-12687.description: Abstract We have investigated the electronic structure of the transition metal oxide Ca 3 Ru 2 O 7 within density-functional theory using the generalized gradient approximation while considering strong Coulomb correlations in the framework of the fully relativistic spin-polarized Dirac linear muffin-tin orbital band-structure method.

arxiv-2411-05498.title: Fate and detectability of rare gas hydride ions in nova ejecta
arxiv-2411-05498.creator: M. Sil, A. Das, R. Das, R. Pandey, A. Faure, H. Wiesemeyer, P. Hily-Blant, F. Lique, P. Caselli
arxiv-2411-05498.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M. Sil, A. Das, R. Das, R. Pandey, A. Faure, H. Wiesemeyer, P. Hily-Blant, F. Lique, P. Caselli. HeH + was the first heteronuclear molecule to form in the metal-free Universe after the Big Bang. The molecule gained significant attention following its first circumstellar detection in the young and dense planetary nebula NGC 7027.

arxiv-2412-16875.title: Swept Volume-Aware Trajectory Planning and MPC Tracking for Multi-Axle Swerve-Drive AMRs Thanks: ∗ Corresponding Author, 1 Equal contribution.
arxiv-2412-16875.creator: Tianxin Hu, Shenghai Yuan, Member, IEEE Ruofei Bai, Xinhang Xu, Yuwen Liao, Fen Liu, Lihua Xie, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2412-16875.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tianxin Hu, Shenghai Yuan, Member, IEEE Ruofei Bai, Xinhang Xu, Yuwen Liao, Fen Liu, Lihua Xie, Fellow, IEEE. Multi-axle autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are set to revolutionize the future of robotics in logistics. As the backbone of next-generation solutions, these robots face a critical challenge: managing and minimizing swept volume during turns while maintaining precise control. Traditional systems designed for standard vehicles often struggle with the complex dynamics of multi-axle configurations, leading to inefficiency and increased safety risk in confined spaces.

arxiv-2511-19612.title: No-go theorems for sequential preparation of two-dimensional chiral states via channel-state correspondence
arxiv-2511-19612.creator: Ruihua Fan, Yantao Wu, Yimu Bao, Zhehao Dai
arxiv-2511-19612.description: Abstract We investigate whether sequential unitary circuits can prepare two-dimensional chiral states, using a correspondence between sequentially prepared states, isometric tensor network states, and one-dimensional quantum channel circuits. We establish two no-go theorems, one for Gaussian fermion systems and one for generic interacting systems.

arxiv-2511-21497.title: Nested ensemble Kalman filter for static parameter inference in nonlinear state-space models
arxiv-2511-21497.creator: Andrew Golightly, Sarah E. Heaps, Chris Sherlock, Laura, E. Wadkin, Darren J. Wilkinson
arxiv-2511-21497.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew Golightly, Sarah E. Heaps, Chris Sherlock, Laura, E. Wadkin, Darren J. Wilkinson. The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is a popular technique for performing inference in state-space models (SSMs), particularly when the dynamic process is high-dimensional. Unlike reweighting methods such as sequential Monte Carlo (SMC, i.e. particle filters), the EnKF leverages either the linear Gaussian structure of the SSM or an approximation thereof, to maintain diversity of the sampled latent states (the so-called ensemble members) via shifting-based updates.

pmc-10526935.title: Design and Experiment of a Biomimetic Duckbill-like Vibration Chain for Physical Weed Control during the Rice Tillering Stage
pmc-10526935.creator: Longyu Fang, Xiwen Luo, Zaiman Wang, Wenwu Yang, Hui Li, Shiyu Song, Haoyang Xie, Jianhao Hu, Weiman Chen, Qinghai Liu
pmc-10526935.description: The widespread use of chemical herbicides has jeopardized concerns about food safety and ecological consequences. To address these issues and reduce reliance on chemical herbicides, a physical weed control device was developed for the tillering stage in paddy fields. This device features a biomimetic duckbill-like vibration chain that effectively controls weed outbreaks.

pmc-10656443.title: Economic valuation of temperature-related mortality attributed to urban heat islands in European cities
pmc-10656443.creator: Wan Ting Katty Huang, Pierre Masselot, Elie Bou-Zeid, Simone Fatichi, Athanasios Paschalis, Ting Sun, Antonio Gasparrini, Gabriele Manoli
pmc-10656443.description: As the climate warms, increasing heat-related health risks are expected, and can be exacerbated by the urban heat island (UHI) effect. UHIs can also offer protection against cold weather, but a clear quantification of their impacts on human health across diverse cities and seasons is still being explored.

pmc-11328022.title: Longitudinal SS-OCT choroidal imaging following thrombosis of the superior ophthalmic vein
pmc-11328022.creator: Mengxi Shen, Prashanth G Iyer, Hao Zhou, Yuxuan Cheng, Jeremy Liu, Omer Trivizki, Ruikang K Wang, Giovanni Gregori, Philip J Rosenfeld
pmc-11328022.description: PurposeTo report longitudinal changes in choroidal thickness and the choroidal vasculature using SS-OCT imaging in a patient with superior ophthalmic vein thrombosis (SOVT).ObservationsIn a 93-year-old woman with a left-sided SOVT, the choroid in the left eye was thickened and the choroidal vessels were dilated both superiorly and inferiorly, with greater changes evident in the inferotemporal region of the choroid.

pmc-11614578.title: A Survey on the Status Quo and Influencing Factors of Health-Related Quality of Life Among Family Caregivers of People with Dementia: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11614578.creator: Hongli Liu, Tengfei Niu, Jiajia Chen, Zhenyu Wu, Taowu Gong, Pengcheng Zhao, Yuhang Zhu, Li Zhang
pmc-11614578.description: BackgroundThis study examined the current state of health-related quality of life among family caregivers of elderly individuals with dementia, analyzing associated influencing factors to provide a foundation for enhancing their health-related quality of life and developing pertinent intervention strategies and measures.

pmc-11627253.title: ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN DIETARY PATTERNS AND PARAMETERS OF OVARIAN RESERVE IN POLISH WOMEN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE
pmc-11627253.creator: Dorota Szczęsna, Kinga Polańska, paweł Radwan, Michał Radwan, Hassan Kassassir, Paulina Mroczek, Joanna Jurewicz
pmc-11627253.description: Objectives:Research investigating the association between reproductive health and diet has predominantly focused on the antenatal and prenatal periods, as well as childbirth in women, and semen quality in men. There is a limited amount of research addressing female fertility assessed as ovarian reserve in relation to diet.

pmc-11716632.title: Tapping into a new hand‐motor biomarker of the dementia continuum ‐ integration and validation in a cognitive clinic
pmc-11716632.creator: Xinyi Wang, Aidan Bindoff, Rebecca J St George, Katherine Lawler, Alastair J Noyce, Quan Bai, Son Tran, Katharine Salmon, James C Vickers, Jane E Alty
pmc-11716632.description: BackgroundThe process for assessing cognitive symptoms in clinic is time consuming, expensive and usually requires multiple clinicians. There is an urgent need for accessible, quick and low‐cost methods to aid identification of people at the early stages of the dementia continuum. Emerging evidence shows that simple hand movement tests could aid risk stratification.

pmc-12372079.title: Is Semaglutide Linked to NAION? A Case Report on a Rare Ocular Complication
pmc-12372079.creator: Dina Lešin Gaćina, Tomislav Vidović, Nikolina Vlajić Oreb, Lovorka Matković, Sonja Jandroković, Toshio Hattori
pmc-12372079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Clinical Significance: Ischemic optic neuropathies (IONs) are significant causes of vision loss resulting from compromised blood flow to the optic nerve. Diabetes mellitus (DM) exacerbates the risk of IONs through chronic hyperglycemia and associated vascular dysfunction. Recently, semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has been linked to ocular complications, including non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), potentially due to the rapid glycemic changes or vascular effects.

pmc-13479319.title: Is there a healthy-food premium? A cross-sectional analysis of the UK online food delivery sector
pmc-13479319.creator: Yuma Asai, Laura Cornelsen, Alexandra Kalbus
pmc-13479319.description: Online food delivery (OFD) platforms account for a growing share of out-of-home meals, but their often poor nutritional quality may worsen diets and related health inequalities. Furthermore, pricing structures within this sector may be systematically incentivizing the selection of higher-calorie items.

pmc-13572599.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations
pmc-13572599.creator: Enrico Mario Alessandro Fassi, Marco Nicolini, Emanuele Saitto, Giorgio Valentini, Elena Casiraghi, Giovanni Grazioso
pmc-13572599.description: IntroductionLarge Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.

pmc-13621600.title: Characteristic flow of different right ventricular outflow tract morphology in repaired tetralogy of fallot patients studied by 4D-flow cardiac magnetic resonance images
pmc-13621600.creator: Auttapol Srivichean, Paweena Chungsomprasong, Yonthakan Sanwong, Thanyarat Phoprom, Chodchanok Vijarnsorn, Karnkawin Patharateeranart, Watcharachai Kangvanskol, Prakul Chanthong, Thita Pacharapakornpong, Ploy Thammasate, Kritvikrom Durongpisitkul, Jarupim Soongswang
pmc-13621600.description: BackgroundRight ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) morphology may influence hemodynamics and suitability for transcatheter pulmonic valve implantation (PPVI) in patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF).MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 120 rTOF patients who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging with 4D-flow analysis. RVOT morphology was classified as tubular, pyramidal, or trapezoid, with inverted pyramidal and concave morphologies absent.
